Dreamerror2026-08-28
Dream's own write command breaks on apostrophes: recommendations.py add failed 3 nights
The dream skill's Step 4 command wraps the JSON payload in single quotes, so any apostrophe in the detail text (for example "operator's" or "the guard's") terminates the shell string early and the add fails with exit 2 (invalid JSON) or exit 127 (command not found). It hit 3 of the last 7 nights: Aug 23, Aug 25, Aug 26. The recommendations still landed only because the agent retried with different quoting. Fix the skill file and any future invocation: write the payload to a temp file and pass it with --json "$(cat /tmp/rec.json)", or escape apostrophes, so the nightly write path never depends on shell quoting.
printf '%s' '{"id":"test","detail":"operator\u0027s"}' > /tmp/rec.json && python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/recommendations.py add --json "$(cat /tmp/rec.json)"
15 min/mo
Why we're suggesting this (3)
  • logs/tool-calls.jsonl: recommendations.py add exit 127 on 2026-08-23T12:33, exit 2 on 2026-08-25T12:36 and 2026-08-26T12:35 - all payloads contain an apostrophe in detail
  • Agent/recommendations.json contains dream-cost-cron-flash, dream-anomaly-gateway-stop-block, dream-session-marathon-context-rot (all created after retries) with apostrophes in their detail text
  • recommendations.py add() returns 2 on JSONDecodeError and the shell returns 127 when the single-quoted string is split by an apostrophe
Dreamcost2026-08-28
QPaint Daily Attention and Overnight Founder Readiness still run on deepseek-v4-pro
The accepted dream-cost-cron-flash fix routed the pulse jobs to deepseek-v4-flash, but two daily client-facing crons still have model:null in cron/jobs.json and fall back to the config default (deepseek-v4-pro). In the last 7 days 4 cron sessions ran on pro at about $0.32 USD total: QPaint Daily Attention (Aug 28, $0.073) and Overnight Founder Readiness (Aug 27 + Aug 28, ~$0.10-0.11 each, 79-97 messages per run). These are fixed-prompt daily jobs that flash already proves it can handle, so setting model to deepseek-v4-flash on both protects headroom on the flat-rate plan at no quality cost.
cd /root/.hermes && python3 -c "import json; p='cron/jobs.json'; d=json.load(open(p)); jobs=d['jobs'] if isinstance(d,dict) and 'jobs' in d else d; [j.update(model='deepseek-v4-flash') for j in jobs if j.get('name') in ('QPaint Daily Attention','Overnight Founder Readiness')]; json.dump(d,open(p,'w'),indent=2)"

4GB/0-swap host is the root cause of gateway kills - swapfile still not applied
The 2026-08-28 8.5h gateway outage was host-level memory exhaustion (SIGKILL): 4GB RAM, zero swap, desktop stack + Chrome + kanban workers starved the box. Mitigations deployed 2026-08-29 (kanban.max_in_progress=3, chrome-idle-close, supervisor daemon) but the root fix remains unapplied: a 2-4GB swapfile. On a 4GB/0-swap host the kernel reaps a process when memory bottoms out - the supervisor can relaunch into a still-starved host, tripping the crash-loop guard. Recommend Josh/Winston add a swapfile (root fix) to eliminate the class of failure entirely.

Gateway guard false-blocks python heredocs that read log files (root cause found)
The Hermes gateway lifecycle filter blocked 14 read-only commands this week (dream.py's top error candidate: terminal::tool_error x101 with this message as its sample), and tonight's dream run was itself blocked 3 times while collecting candidates. Root cause now confirmed: the guard's referenced-script walk reads files opened inside python heredocs / -c blocks, and any file whose contents contain the trigger phrase - logs/tool-calls.jsonl (which stores the guard's own block messages), Agent/Infrastructure.md, dashboard HTML - trips it even for pure reads. Verified against cron/lifecycle_guard.py on 2026-08-27: direct shell reads (cat/grep/tail) of the same files pass; only python heredocs opening them are blocked. Fix upstream in lifecycle_guard.py: skip non-executable data files (.jsonl/.md/.html) in the referenced-script walk, or apply the existing data-sink exemption to it. Until then, read log/data files with read_file/search_files/cat/grep, not python heredocs.
grep -c "referenced script cannot" /root/.hermes/logs/tool-calls.jsonl
